extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of journalism/media studies; researchers of news production and newsroom organization
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the evaluative dimensions and production standards underlying newsmaking (e.g., newsworthiness, objectivity, sourcing, narrative forms, newsroom routines, technical conventions) as presented in an academic study of news production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness, 6, 8, 15, 46, 139, 212; interpretive approach to, 183-84; negotiation of, 31-38, 211.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiated in editorial processes (see negotiation of news-worthiness 31-38); treated via typifications/categories of news and constitution of issues as topics (see Categories of news; Constitution of issues or occurrences as topics 133-36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of news / Typifications (hard, soft, spot, continuing, developing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of news, 47-50; as typifications, see Typifications; see also Continuing news; Developing news; Hard news; Soft news; Spot news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different story-types/typifications (hard news, soft/feature, spot, continuing, developing) structure newsroom selection, planning, and presentation (see continuing news 56-58; developing news 54-56; spot news 53-54).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity / Neutrality / Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectivity: emergence of, 158-61; ideology and, 177-79; Neutrality (impartiality), 83, 146, 152; news film’s claim to, 110, 115, 119-21, 124.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a professional norm and strategic ritual; related to factual presentation, fairness, and claims made by news forms (see Fairness; Facticity; Facts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facts / Facticity / Verification of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts (factual news), 210-11; credibilty and, 83, 84, 87; definition of facts, 82; finding, 83, 101-103; verification of, 83-86; mutually self-validating facts, 86, 87, 93-95.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on finding and verifying facts as central to professionalism; processes include sourcing, corroboration, and distinction between facts and interpretation (see Facts and Sources, imputing, relocating facticity 90-92).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources: access, legitimation, hoarding, reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources: access to the media, 133-34, 141; centralized sources of information, 18-23, 81, 87, 94n, 210, 214; hoarding, 73-74, 78, 79; proven reliability of, 93; legitimated sources, 92, 210.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source selection and relationships (institutionalized, legitimated, reliable) are criteria for what becomes news; source hoarding/sharing affects access and story framing (see Knowing sources 68-73; Sharing of information 73-80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism and professional norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Professionalism, 64, 101, 105, 166, 203, 210, 212-13, 215; emergence and growth of, 158-61; fairness and, 174; narrative construction and, 105-106, 127-128.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional norms (craft consciousness, stock of knowledge at hand, autonomy) shape selection, verification, narrative construction, and organizational flexibility (see Professional autonomy; Craft consciousness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional autonomy and organizational constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Autonomy, professional, 65, 74, 76, 78, 79, 106, 107; Organizational flexibility, 31, 45, 132; professionalism and City Hall bureau example, 66-81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of reporter/editor autonomy and organizational flexibility affects sourcing, story negotiation, and coverage priorities; routines, contracts, and managerial roles moderate autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial negotiation and daily routines (editorial conference, planning, deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial conference, daily, 33-34, 37, 41; Daily tempo of newsmaking, 41-44; Deadlines: missed, 72-73; Planning, across days, 41, 44-45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily editorial routines (conferences, scheduling, planning, rhythm) determine what can be covered and how stories are developed; missed deadlines and planning affect coverage depth and type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead structure and informational writing form
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead-documentation structure, 100, 101, 103; Lead sentence, 100, 101, 105; Informational mode of newspaper writing, 1877.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal expectations for news leads and documentation shape what counts as acceptable reporting and how facts are presented vs. interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative forms / News narrative / Presentation modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative forms or modes, 100-103, 105, 106, 125-28, 132, 139, 215, 217; News narrative (news story), 104-32; Narrative, finding facts and, 101-102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of narrative form (story as accessible craft skill) influences fact selection, order, and perceived facticity; narrative construction is a professional skill (see Craft skill).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frames / Frame analysis / Construction of reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame, news as, 1, 7, 23, 25, 38, 50, 58, 99, 103, 156, 192-95, 216; Frame analysis, 192-94; Constructed reality: news as, 12, 182-97.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames organize which aspects of occurrences become news and how they are interpreted; frame analysis is an interpretive approach to evaluate news construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credibility pertains to sources, facts, presentation, and institutional reputation; credible presentation depends on verification, sourcing, and professional form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness / Balance / First Amendment and Fairness Doctrine considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness: newspapers and, 161; Fairness Doctrine, 83m, 171-74; First Amendment, 165-76; Freedom of speech and access to media, 165-76, 168-72.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/regulatory standards (Fairness Doctrine, licensing, First Amendment) and fairness norms constrain content, sourcing, and editorial decisions; balance and opportunity to reply are evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page one / Front-page selection and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: First page, see Page one; Page one (first page), 33-37; Sigal’s study of balance on, 33, 35-37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement on front page and balance of topics are evaluative indicators of news priority and perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of resources / Reporter dispersion / Territorial and topical specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of resources, typifications and, 51-54; Reporters, dispersion of (placement), 18-31; Territorial editors, 30-33; Topical specialization, 29-30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How news organizations allocate reporters in space/time and by specialty (territorial, topical) influences coverage breadth, depth, and what becomes visible as news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of information / Reportorial cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperation, reportorial, 77-80; Sharing of information by reporters, 23, 73-80; with competitors and within organizations, 75-80.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional courtesy and information-sharing practices affect timeliness, duplication, and the shape of stories; hoarding vs. sharing is an operational criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing / Timeliness / Immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediacy, 15; 'Timeliness,' 51; Live coverage, 42-43; Temporal synchronization of reporters’ working hours, 42, 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speed and synchronization with events/institutions are criteria for news value; live coverage and temporal concentration influence perceived newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/visual conventions for television news film (camera work, shots, editing, continuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera work in news film, 131-32; placement, 111-15; range, 116-21, 123; Shots, standard, 120-24, 130; Editing, 106, 124-26; Continuity in news film, 128; Filmic conventions and codes, 108-109, 116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual and editing conventions (standard shots, continuity, codes/symbols) are criteria for how television news constructs facticity, involvement, and neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexicality and reflexivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexicality, 53n, 86, 88, 189-92, 198, 201; Reflexivity, 167, 189-92; Public character of news, reflexivity and indexicality and, 189-91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to indexical signs and reflexive acknowledgment of news’ public role shape claims about what counts as evidence and facticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimation / Objectification of institutions and knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Legitimation: of institutions, 103, 215; of sources, 94n; Objectification, 87; of knowledge, 58-59, 217; Legitimated newsmakers, 115, 123, 130.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News often confers or relies on institutional legitimation; objectification of meanings and knowledge by institutions is central to what is presented as authoritative in news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation ethics and legal constraints (libel, property, licensing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Libel suits, 83-84; Licenses, television, 170-71; Property rights and privately generated information, 73; Right to know, 165-66, 174, 176.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal risks (libel), licensing, and property/right-to-know considerations constrain reporting choices and are criteria for responsible production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution of issues as news topics (agenda setting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitution of issues or occurrences as topics, 133-36; Agenda setting, 2; Political agenda, setting of, 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How occurrences are framed into issues (agenda-setting processes) is a criterion for determining public salience and news selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credible presentation of emotion and involvement in visual news
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotion (feeling), news film and, 115, 119-20, 123-24; Involvement, news film and, 115, 116, 118, 119, 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of visual/emotional cues must serve credible representation; choices about showing emotion or involvement affect perceived objectivity and audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routines, rhythm, and tempo of newsmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Routines (routinization), 40n, 50, 57, 58, 212; Rhythm: of daily life, 211; Tempo, daily, 41-44; Planning across days, 41, 44-45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational rhythms and routinized procedures structure what can be covered and how thoroughly; tempo is an operational constraint and evaluative factor.
